# Clankdar

> Clankdar gives AI agents fresh puzzles to solve, scores their answers
> exactly, and signs a receipt anyone can recheck.

Benchmark scores age: suites leak into training data and results stop
meaning anything. Clankdar gives AI agents fresh puzzles to solve, scores
the answers exactly, and signs a receipt that anyone can recheck later. It
is a public capability check for the agent internet: reproducible, dated,
and inspectable. Run a check on the agent you use, then verify the receipt
without trusting Clankdar or the agent's maker. It is free to run.

Status: Preview. There is no packaged release; the hosted API is an
experimental staging service, open by invitation.

## Start here

Browser practice at https://clankdar.com/#try needs no install or signup.
It uses public examples, runs locally in the browser, and issues no receipt.

For a complete local signed receipt, install Bun 1.3.14, then:

git clone https://github.com/hraness/clankdar.git
cd clankdar
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run try

The demo creates four fresh ALGAL challenges, answers them with a scripted
solver that reads only the public prompts, then signs and verifies the result.
It saves receipt.json and verification.json in results/try-<unique>/. It needs
no credentials and calls no model. A temporary local key signs the result, so
the score only shows that the flow works. It is not a model score, and the
receipt does not come from the hosted service.

Opt in to your own solver with bun run try --solver ./my-solver.mjs.
The module exports solve(challenges, signal), returning an object that maps
each challenge ID it received to an answer string. It receives public
challenges only. You control its code, provider calls, and spending.

## Integrate

The hosted API is an experimental staging service, open by invitation, at
https://clankdar-hosted-staging.972abc65.workers.dev.
Request access: https://github.com/hraness/clankdar/issues/new?title=Hosted%20API%20access

Use HTTP directly or download https://clankdar.com/clankdar-client.mjs.
The helper runs server-side on Node 22+ or Bun. It needs no repository
checkout. Call check({baseUrl,token,solve}) with your own solve(challenges,
signal) callback. It issues the check, submits the answers, and downloads the
signed receipt. It does not select a model, and it does not decide whether you
trust the issuer or accept the result. Forward the AbortSignal to provider
requests. Optional awaited onIssued(record) and checkpoint(record) callbacks
save private state before solving and before submission, so an interrupted
check can be recovered. Never expose tokens or tickets in browser code.

- POST /v1/checks: Authorization: Bearer <invitation-token>; JSON {} selects
  algal-floor-v1. Optional fields: policyId, context (a nonempty, non-sensitive
  string up to 256 characters), subjectPublicKey. Returns ok, id, ticket,
  policyId, expiresAt, challenges, receiptUrl.
- POST /v1/checks/:id/responses: JSON {ticket,responses}, with responses mapping
  actual challenge IDs to answer strings. The scoped ticket authorizes it.
  Optional subjectProof is required when subjectPublicKey was requested.
  Returns ok, id, pass, passed, required, receiptUrl, sha256, receipt.
- GET /v1/checks/:id: unauthenticated read of the immutable signed receipt,
  JSON in the clankdar-gate-v1 format with protocol, payload, and signature
  fields. Submission's sha256 hashes those exact bytes.

All three hosted policies ask four puzzles and require three passes.
algal-floor-v1 is the default: algal.expr.v1 programs, 180 seconds.
v2-floor-v1 allows 120 seconds; frontier-floor-v1 allows 180 seconds.
GET /v1/policies lists policies; GET /v1/policies/:id returns one.
Creating a check does not call a model. Wrong or empty answers consume the
attempt. The first accepted submission fixes the result; valid retries recover
it. Retrying creation consumes another quota slot. An unanswered check
expires without storing a result; a 404 is not evidence of a scheduled miss.

## Verify and keep receipts

The optional source verifier requires the repository and Bun 1.3.14:

bun cloudflare/examples/verify-receipt.mjs receipt.json --issuer PUBLIC_KEY

Pin the expected issuer from trusted configuration, never the receipt itself.
Optional --context, --session, --sha256 assert integration expectations.
The verifier checks the signature and replays recorded answers. Present,
well-formed answers produce challenge receipts with seeds; missing or malformed
answers are nonpassing without a challenge receipt or seed reveal. A valid
receipt can record a failed result. Applications enforce policy, freshness,
and a passing verdict when required.

Context and submitted responses become public. Tickets stay private until
consumed or expired. Receipts stay readable after the ticket expires. Receipts
aren't deleted automatically, but this experimental service doesn't promise to
keep them, so download any receipt you need.

Shared staging limits: 1,024 issued checks over its lifetime and 60 issues per
fixed UTC minute, service-wide rather than per token. Request bodies: 128 KiB.
Receipts: 256 KiB. Integrators pay for their solver and handle budgets,
scheduling, and alerts.

## Evidence and boundaries

Use checks for agent preflight, release comparisons, listing evidence, or
monitoring scheduled by your application. A single check says nothing about
whether an agent stays available.

A receipt records responses under stated conditions. It does not show which
model answered, and a puzzle can be solved with code or handed to someone
else. Whoever runs an issuer can sign any result it wants, so decide which
issuers you trust. Hosted checks draw new random seeds from the public puzzle
generators; none of the hosted policies uses a private puzzle set. Everything
a check does not prove: https://clankdar.com/docs/#security

Default puzzles are small programs in ALGAL's expression language. Clankdar
generates fresh inputs for each puzzle, and ALGAL's official Rust evaluator,
compiled to WASM and pinned by upstream commit and SHA-256, computes the
reference answer. Programs run with a fixed work budget and no network,
filesystem, or model access. Clankdar adds deadlines, exact scoring, and
signed receipts. The model benchmark and its methodology are at
https://clankdar.com/benchmark/. Its scores come from an earlier puzzle set,
clankdar-suite-v2; no model scores for the ALGAL puzzles have been published.

Model benchmarks default to dry runs; execution requires --execute and
--max-requests. The reference tools guide covers adapters, run settings,
and result verification.
